headline: Funding flows. Contracts prioritize speed. Talent shifts.
deck: This week saw significant funding rounds and strategic hires, reflecting the evolving landscape of aerospace and defense.

stories.head: Skyroot raises $60 million for launch ambitions
stories.body: Skyroot Aerospace has secured $60 million ahead of its inaugural orbital launch attempt, reflecting investor confidence in its capabilities. The funding will be pivotal as it gears up to compete in the increasingly crowded launch market, where every dollar counts as much as every launch. With this cash injection, Skyroot aims to solidify its position in the Indian space sector.
stories.soWhat: Investors are clearly betting on the next wave of launch providers, but the real question is whether Skyroot can deliver results or just more promises.

stories.head: National security contracts favor speed over cost
stories.body: A recent shift in national security contracting priorities now emphasizes speed over price, a change that could reshape bidding strategies. This comes as the Pentagon seeks faster delivery of capabilities amid rising global tensions. Companies that can deliver quickly will likely see an uptick in contracts, while those focused solely on cost may find themselves sidelined.
stories.soWhat: This is a refreshing pivot for the defense sector, but it may lead to a new set of problems if rushed contracts result in subpar performance.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly has successfully raised $190 million in its Series C round, achieving a valuation of $1.6 billion. This funding will enhance its capabilities in co-orbital security and space domain awareness, areas that are becoming increasingly critical for national defense. With the DoD's growing interest in satellite security, True Anomaly is well-positioned to capitalize on government contracts.
stories.soWhat: The funding reflects a broader trend where revenue generation is prioritized over mere technological advancement, a signal that the market is maturing.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on Anthropic's partnership with SpaceX
watchlist.body: If Anthropic adopts SpaceX's orbital data centers, it could redefine cloud computing in space, impacting traditional data centers.

watchlist.title: Watch for Starfighters' air-launch platform progress
watchlist.body: With Blue Origin veterans on board, Starfighters may accelerate its air-launch platform, potentially shaking up the small satellite launch market.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN extension may signal more defense contracts
watchlist.body: The $480M extension on the TITAN program could lead to further lucrative contracts in the defense sector, as Palantir expands its footprint.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser variant could attract attention
watchlist.body: Clearing the critical design review is just the start; the real test will be whether it meets military needs effectively.

talent.statLabel: Week-over-week growth in resumes from primes to Series B/C
talent.head: Talent is leaving big-aero — and it's not about money
talent.body: Compensation is not the gating factor. The complaint, almost universally, is schedule risk — the inability to ship anything quickly, the half-decade gap between joining and seeing flight hardware, the meeting that exists to schedule the meeting. The startups absorbing this talent will, in two years, be hard to compete with on a level playing field.
